h1: The 8 Best 2-Drawer Nightstands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 two-drawer nightstands compared on capacity, charging, LED options and finish, from a 100 lb Yoobure to a matched pair.
summary: The Yoobure is the best two-drawer nightstand overall, the only one here with FCC and ETL certification and a 100 lb rating. The Huuger LED model is the pick for lighting fans, and the rustic Huuger gives you USB-C without the light show. The Nathan James set suits a styled pair, while the Sweetcrispy covers tight budgets.
intro: A bedside table has a small job list: hold a lamp, hold a phone charger, hide the clutter. Where two-drawer models split is in the extras around those drawers, such as built-in power, mood lighting, rated capacity and whether you are furnishing one side of the bed or both.

Our editors reviewed eight current models from spec sheets and listings. Seven are single tables and one is a matched pair. Ranking weighs power and weight capacity first, then frame materials and safety certification, then finish and extras like LED strips. Where a listing leaves out a figure, the entry says so instead of guessing.

products.name: Yoobure 2-Drawer Vintage Brown Nightstand, FCC & ETL Certified, 100 lb Capacity
products.verdict: FCC and ETL certified charging with a 100 lb capacity rating.
products.description:
The Yoobure is a 15.75 by 11.81 by 23.62 inch table built from engineered wood and steel, with two fabric drawers. Power comes from two USB ports and two outlets on a 6.5 ft cord, and the listing names both FCC and ETL certification alongside a 100 lb capacity.

Those two credentials decide the top spot. It is the only table in the ranking that documents electrical certification, and its weight rating is double that of the Furologee and well past the other charging models. The Huuger tables beat it on lighting and USB-C, but neither lists a safety mark or a capacity figure we can lean on.

Buy it for a bedside that gets used hard: lamp, phone, tablet and a stack of books. The caveat is that charging is basic, with no USB-C listed, and the fabric drawers suit small items rather than heavy ones.

products.name: Huuger 2-Drawer Black Nightstand with 60,000-Color LED and USB-C
products.verdict: 60,000 colors, 12 scene modes, music sync and USB-C in a black table.
products.description:
The Huuger black nightstand is the showpiece of the group. It measures 15.7 by 11.8 by 23.6 inches in P2 particleboard with a powder-coated steel frame, offers two AC outlets plus one USB-A and one USB-C port, and adds an LED with 60,000 colors, 12 scene modes, music sync and app control.

It lands second because nothing else here matches the lighting feature set, and it is one of only two models with USB-C. What keeps it behind the Yoobure is paperwork: no certification and no capacity rating are listed, which matters for a table carrying live wiring.

Buy it if you want ambient lighting built into the furniture and enjoy tuning it from a phone. Skip it if you prefer a plain table, because the LED system is an extra layer of app dependence that does nothing for storage.

products.name: Huuger 2-Drawer Rustic Brown Nightstand with USB-C
products.verdict: The same Huuger charging layout in rustic brown with a stain-resistant top.
products.description:
This rustic brown Huuger strips away the light show and keeps the useful part. It is 15.7 by 11.8 by 23.6 inches, built from P2 particleboard on a powder-coated steel frame, with two fabric drawers, two AC outlets, a USB-A port, a USB-C port and a stain-resistant top.

Third place reflects a clean trade. Compared with the black Huuger above, you lose the LED but also lose the app and the extra feature to troubleshoot. Compared with the WLIVE and Furologee below, you gain USB-C, which neither of them lists.

It suits a rustic bedroom where phones and earbuds need a daily charge. The caveat is that the listing gives no weight capacity, so keep the load light, and the drawers are fabric rather than wood.

products.name: WLIVE 2-Drawer White Nightstand with RGB LED, 3 USB Ports, 55 lb Capacity
products.verdict: Three USB ports and two outlets with a 55 lb capacity and a waterproof top.
products.description:
The WLIVE white nightstand is the tallest in the lineup at 25.19 inches, with a footprint of 15.67 by 11.73 inches in MDF and steel. It carries three USB ports, two of them on the front and one at the back, plus two AC outlets, an app-controlled RGB LED, a waterproof top and a 55 lb rating.

It sits fourth because the port count and tabletop protection are strong, yet the capacity trails the Yoobure by nearly half and no safety mark appears. Against the Furologee below, it offers more connections and a sturdier rating, which justifies the gap.

Choose it for a white bedroom with several devices charging overnight. The catch is that the LED relies on the iStrip+ app, so anyone who wants simple on and off control may find it fussy.
products.idealFor: White bedrooms with lots of devices.
products.skipIf: You do not want an app.

products.name: Furologee 2-Drawer White Nightstand with S-Hooks, 50 lb Capacity
products.verdict: Two shelves, two drawers and S-hooks, at a lower 22.25 inch height.
products.description:
Furologee makes the low-bed answer. The white table is 11.75 by 14.96 by 22.25 inches in engineered wood and metal, with two fabric drawers, two tiers of open shelving, two outlets, two USB ports and a pair of included S-hooks. Capacity is rated at 50 lb.

It ranks fifth because the shorter height and extra shelves solve a specific problem, but the weight rating sits below the WLIVE and Yoobure and it lacks USB-C. The shelves do give it better storage flexibility than the Huuger models, which rely on the drawers alone.

It is a good match for low platform beds where a tall table would tower over the mattress. Skip it if you need a higher surface, since the 22.25 inch height is among the shortest charging options here.

products.name: WLIVE 2-Drawer Rustic Brown Nightstand
products.verdict: No electronics, four self-leveling feet and about 15 minutes of assembly.
products.description:
This WLIVE rustic brown model is the simplest table with real finish quality. It measures 15.7 by 11.8 by 20.9 inches, uses MDF with a steel frame, and has two fabric drawers, a water-resistant wooden top and four self-leveling feet. There are no charging ports.

Sixth place comes from the missing power, not from poor design. With no wiring there is nothing to certify and little that can fail, and assembly is listed at about 15 minutes. The Sweetcrispy below costs less but is shorter and narrower in function, so this one edges it.

Pick it for a minimal bedside where a power strip or wall outlet already handles charging. Skip it if you want to plug a phone straight into the furniture, because it offers no outlets or USB at all.

products.name: Sweetcrispy 2-Drawer White Nightstand
products.verdict: The cheapest here, with end-stop drawers and a water-resistant top.
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy is the price leader, listed under $25. It measures 18 by 11.8 by 20 inches with a metal frame and engineered wood, two fabric drawers with arch handles, end-stop drawer design and a water-resistant top. Capacity is 44 lb.

It takes seventh place because it is the plainest and shortest table here, with the lowest weight rating and no charging. The savings are real, though, and the end-stop drawers keep the fabric bins from sliding out, a small touch that cheaper tables often skip.

Buy it for a guest room, dorm or first apartment where cost matters most. The caveat is the 20 inch height, which can look stubby next to a standard bed, and the 44 lb rating leaves little room for heavy decor.

products.name: Nathan James Harper Oak Brown Nightstand Set of 2, Lifetime Warranty
products.verdict: A set of two with a lifetime warranty and a 100-day money back offer.
products.description:
Nathan James sells the Harper as a set of two tables, each 16 by 16 by 23.5 inches. The build combines MDF, particleboard and pinewood legs, with two easy-glide drawers per table, brass hardware and tapered legs. The offer includes a lifetime warranty and a 100-day money back window.

It ranks last only because the criteria here reward power and capacity, and this set has neither charging nor a stated weight rating. As furniture it is the most design-led option, and the price covers two tables, which makes it less expensive per piece than it looks at the $200 to $500 level.

Buy it for a styled bedroom that needs a matching pair. Skip it if you want built-in outlets or a narrow footprint, since the square 16 inch top takes more floor space than the slimmer models above.
products.idealFor: A styled pair of bedside tables.
products.skipIf: You need power or a narrow table.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is the weight a table is rated to hold, and here it runs from 44 lb on the Sweetcrispy to 100 lb on the Yoobure. A lamp, a clock, books and a drink add up faster than most buyers expect. Look for a stated figure in the listing bullets and aim for at least 50 lb.

Any furniture with built-in wiring should carry a recognized safety mark, because it sits beside a sleeping person all night. The Yoobure alone lists FCC and ETL here. Search the listing title and bullets for the certification names, and treat silence as a reason to ask or choose another table.

Ports decide how useful a charging table is. A phone, a tablet and a lamp need three connections, and some models give you only two. The WLIVE lists three USB ports and two outlets, while the Huuger tables add USB-C. Count the outlets and USB ports in the spec bullets, and confirm whether USB-C is included.

Height matters because a nightstand should sit near the mattress top for easy reach. This group runs from 20 inches on the Sweetcrispy to 25.19 inches on the WLIVE. Measure your mattress top from the floor, then compare it with the listed height. Low platform beds suit the Furologee at 22.25 inches.

Fabric drawers are light, cheap and removable, but they hold far less than wood or metal slides. Every single table here uses them, while the Nathan James set offers easy-glide drawers. Read the capacity figure and think of the drawers as storage for small items like chargers, glasses and notebooks rather than heavy gear.

faq.q: What is the best two-drawer nightstand?
faq.a: The Yoobure is our top pick. It combines FCC and ETL certification, two USB ports, two outlets and a 100 lb capacity in one table. The Huuger black model is the better choice if you care more about lighting and USB-C than certification.

Yes, on the Huuger tables. Both the black LED model and the rustic brown one list a USB-C port alongside USB-A and two AC outlets. The Yoobure lists two USB ports without saying whether either one is USB-C.

For small items such as chargers, glasses and a journal, they work fine. The limit is the stated capacity rather than the drawer fabric itself, which runs from 44 lb on the Sweetcrispy to 100 lb on the Yoobure.

ETL is an electrical safety mark that shows a product was evaluated against recognized standards. The Yoobure is the only listing here that names FCC and ETL, which makes it the safer choice for a table with built-in outlets and USB ports.

faq.q: Is a set better than a single?
faq.a: A set looks better when you need a matched look on both sides of the bed, and the Nathan James Harper adds a lifetime warranty. For a single bedside or a power-first setup, the Yoobure or a Huuger fits better.

The WLIVE rustic brown and the Sweetcrispy both list about 15 minutes of assembly, making them the quickest of the group. Tables with outlets and LED wiring, like the Huuger and Yoobure, may take longer to put together and connect.

finalTake: Choose the Yoobure if the table will carry real daily use, since it pairs certified charging with the highest weight rating here. Pick a Huuger for USB-C or lighting, the WLIVE or Furologee for specific bed heights, and the Nathan James when you want two matching tables backed by a lifetime warranty. Check the capacity and port count on the listing before you buy.
